subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is an example of MITIGATION of climate change rather than adaptation?
options: Switching to renewable energy to cut emissions
questions.explain: Mitigation reduces the causes (emissions); adaptation copes with the effects.

questions.q: The middle-latitude atmospheric circulation cell, between the Hadley and Polar cells, is the:
questions.explain: The Ferrel cell operates at mid-latitudes between the Hadley and Polar cells.

questions.q: Which gas released by burning fossil fuels is the main HUMAN cause of recent climate change?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels is the chief human-enhanced greenhouse gas.

questions.q: Which monitoring method helps PREDICT a volcanic eruption?
options: Measuring changes in gas emissions and ground bulging with seismometers
questions.explain: Rising gas output, ground swelling and small tremors warn that an eruption may be near.

questions.q: Which condition is REQUIRED for a tropical storm to form?
options: Sea-surface temperatures of at least about 27 degrees C
questions.explain: Tropical storms need warm ocean water of around 27 degrees C or more to provide energy.

questions.q: Why do many people continue to live in tectonically active areas?
options: Fertile volcanic soils and geothermal energy
There is no other land available anywhere
questions.explain: Volcanic areas offer fertile soils, geothermal energy, tourism and mineral resources.

questions.q: Volcanoes and earthquakes are mostly found:
options: In the centre of tectonic plates
questions.explain: Tectonic hazards concentrate at plate boundaries where plates interact.

questions.q: The most intense winds and heaviest rain in a tropical storm occur in the:
questions.explain: The eyewall, the ring of towering clouds around the eye, has the strongest winds and rain.

questions.q: Which is a LONG-TERM response to a tectonic disaster?
questions.explain: Rebuilding to better standards takes months or years and is a long-term response.

questions.q: Surface winds blowing towards the equator from the high-pressure belts are called the:
questions.explain: Trade winds blow from the subtropical high-pressure belts towards the equatorial low.

questions.q: Which scale measures earthquake magnitude on a logarithmic scale, so each step is ten times greater in amplitude?
questions.explain: The Richter scale is logarithmic, so each whole number is a tenfold increase in measured amplitude.

questions.q: Convection currents that move tectonic plates occur in which layer?
questions.explain: Heat-driven convection currents in the semi-molten mantle drag the plates above.

questions.q: When two continental plates collide at a collision margin, the result is usually:
questions.explain: Neither continental plate subducts easily, so sediment and crust crumple upward into fold mountains.

questions.q: Effects of an earthquake are often worse in a LIC than a HIC mainly because:
options: HICs sit further from plate margins
Buildings are less able to withstand shaking and emergency services are weaker
LIC earthquakes are always higher magnitude
questions.explain: Poorer building quality and limited emergency resources increase impacts in LICs.

questions.q: Which is a NATURAL cause of climate change?
options: Variations in the Sun's output and volcanic eruptions
questions.explain: Solar variation, orbital changes and volcanic activity are natural climate drivers.

questions.q: Which is the hottest and densest layer at the centre of the Earth?
questions.explain: The inner core is a solid ball of iron and nickel and is the hottest, densest layer.

questions.q: In which atmospheric cell does cold air sink at the poles, creating high pressure?
questions.explain: In the Polar cell, very cold dense air sinks at the poles forming high pressure.

questions.q: Which is a method of earthquake PROTECTION rather than prediction?
questions.explain: Earthquake-resistant building design protects people, whereas monitoring is prediction.

questions.q: Which is an example of ADAPTATION to climate change?
options: Using solar panels instead of coal
Building sea walls to cope with rising sea levels
questions.explain: Adaptation means coping with effects, such as defending coasts against higher seas.

questions.q: The calm, clear centre of a tropical storm is called the:
questions.explain: The eye is the calm low-pressure centre, surrounded by the violent eyewall.

questions.q: The Saffir-Simpson scale is used to measure the:
options: Strength of tropical storms by wind speed
questions.explain: The Saffir-Simpson scale rates tropical storms from category 1 to 5 by their wind speeds.

questions.q: A tsunami can be triggered when an earthquake occurs:
options: Under the sea, displacing a large volume of water
At the centre of a plate only
questions.explain: An undersea earthquake suddenly displaces water, generating tsunami waves.
